Overrated:

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. I'm kind of a LoZ fan (played through about a dozen of those games, OoT is my favourite game of all time). However I'm one of those fans who are extra critical of new entries of my beloved franchises, and not one of those fans who will eat up whatever they sell to me just because it's yet another entry. For brevity's sake I'll just jot down my issues with the game, but my points might still be long because I have a lot to say about this game:

Negatives:

- Big open world that feels empty (isn't helped by lack of music either)

- Big open world isn't fun to explore either thanks to Link's horrible stamina (moar like Out of Breath in the Wild m i rite guyz?!) and the way to call your horse is not as accessible as it was in the past titles

- Not a lot of side activities to do (there's mini dungeons where you can get items to upgrade your health and stamina, and some short random activities you can do when coming across certain NPCs that give you items to upgrade your inventory space)

- Only 4 big-ish dungeons instead of the classic 8, and they weren't nearly as interesting

- Story is too simple even by LoZ standards (bad thing happened in past, castle is where bad guy is, go to 4 places to weaken castle barrier, go face bad guy)

- Voice acting only in cutscenes and missing in some of the most illogical places (for instance there's a bird man NPC that sings you tales, but when that happens only music plays and there's only subtitles). Also I really don't like the English voice of Zelda. She sounds too whiny

- Terrible performance on the WiiU (choppy and stuttery a lot of the time, will even freeze for a second or so under certain conditions such as knocking down a big enemy (probably overwhelms the weak CPU with the ragdoll physics calculations), kind of expected though as this game is too technically ambitious for such weak hardware)

- Poor performance leads to an inferior and not fun combat experience

- Weapon durability too low especially at the beginning, with no way to repair weapons (weapons just shatter, no blacksmiths in the game either)

- WiiU touchpad features completely scrapped, probably to achieve parity with switch version

Now the positives:

+ Cel shaded graphics look nice

+ Technologically impressive (mainly with the use of physics in many things in such a large scale game)

+ Interesting additions to combat (parrying, dodging to slow down time temporarily)

+ Interesting additions for exploration as well (able to climb almost anything, shield surfing)

+ Towns are well made (feels like a LoZ game again whenever you enter one of these, what with the music, town design, unique NPCs)

+ Some good and tough enemy encounters (particularly the laser beam shooting things and those huge centaur guys)

Overall this game was like a 7/10 for me. It's good, but not great. Especially for a LoZ game.

Other games I found overrated this generation would be red dead redemption 2 (too slow, shooting mechanics sucked, too much pozz, good overall story though, great graphics, physics, atmosphere) and uncharted 4 (first 1/3rd was great, rest of it was very poorly paced, unlikeable nigress character who is literally untouchable, meh gameplay, good conclusion to Drake's story at least).

As for an underrated game, I can't really think of one this generation, but The Darkness on the xbox 360 and PS3 is one. Great dark atmosphere, well written story and characters, interesting gameplay. It's not without its flaws (some of the animations looked odd, shooting could've felt a bit better, main character runs too slow), but overall I really liked it. I'd love to see a proper remake of this game someday, but considering how little attention it got I don't think it'll ever happen. The lack of a PC version certainly doesn't help either.

Oh man, Skyward Sword was another disappointment for me. If I had two words to describe it, it would be "wasted potential." It was probably the only Zelda game with full 3d flight, and yet they did nothing interesting with it. Could've had lots of towns, villages, areas of interest, etc in the map, but all we got were a couple of settlements on small rocks, a couple of heart piece locations, and maybe a dungeon or two (can't exactly remember).

There was a lot of padding too. I remember 1 filler activity made 0 sense at all story wise. It was some dumb musical note collection game that involved swimming which you had to do so that you could get some story related item. This blue dragon character makes you do it to earn her trust or some shit. What makes no sense about it is that this bitch is only alive is because Link cured her illness a couple of dungeons ago!

Also there was a game breaking but with no fix for it I believe. You just had to ensure you don't progress the game in the way that will trigger this bug, which someone at my work unfortunately did in his playthrough and he hasn't gotten back to it since.

I wasn't fan of the controls either. I had a lot of issues with the swings registering properly, so it made fighting those enemies who change their shield positions especially annoying.

The game did have pretty good graphics and music though, so I'll give it that. Also the desert portion of the game with time travel mechanic was phenomenal. If the rest of the game was as high quality as this area it would've been a solid 9/10 game for me and easily one of the best Zelda games.

Despite all the issues I still liked it a bit better than BotW. "At least it can't be worse than Skyward Sword" I foolishly thought to myself. I just hope the next BotW game will be more interesting, but I won't be holding my breath (pun not intended).
